claims.claim: The dependency retry gate treats commands with differing runs of whitespace inside quoted arguments as the same command, allowing a different argument to use an existing retry allowance.
claims.trigger: Two dependency-classified shell calls in the same active root within the grace period differ only by whitespace runs, including quoted argument content
claims.exceptions: Force/reference classifications are handled before this gate; this does not bypass those ask decisions. No actual install was run.
claims.enforcement_effect: Effective retry-identity relaxation; one prior denial can authorize a different quoted argument at the hook level.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Prior actions call the accepted retry identical; they do not register equivalence of different quoted argument content.
The fixed time window and lack of due-diligence verification differ from lossy normalization. BF0065 quotes the same code, but its action and scenario are an immediate identical retry.

claims.comparison_reason: All-three claims focus on timing or identical retry without verification. Source regex is quote-insensitive. The pure-copy PROBES/L1_retry_key_probe.mjs actually classified both quoted-path variants as dependencies and returned the same key.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: npm install with a quoted file path containing two spaces is denied. A subsequent install of the different path containing one space has the same key and takes the allowance.
claims.open_question: Does this verified retry-identity relaxation warrant a distinct effective-constraint record or only an implementation defect note?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Executable and modality families examine identity expectations and actual state consumption; the pure probe already verifies classification/key collision.

claims.claim: When Git state is unavailable, the Stop hook asks for manual seed, migration and test co-change checks.
claims.trigger: changedFiles returns null because the active project is outside Git or Git acquisition fails
claims.exceptions: Advisory systemMessage; same no-Git fingerprint suppresses repeated messages; stop_hook_active exits early.
claims.enforcement_effect: Manual-check fallback request, not the ordinary blocking co-change output.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Primary describes manual checks but marks the range implementation.
Replica explicitly states that outside Git the hook asks for manual seed, migration and test checks and links their actions. RULE0045 also states advisory-only outside Git.

claims.comparison_reason: The semantic union includes all raw dispositions and resolved coverage, so a primary omission does not establish novelty when replica explicitly represents the fallback.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: Stop in a non-Git workspace yields a manual-check message, a case already described by replica.
